We did in parallel identify some other bug (https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-19994) which seems to have similar symptoms, ie, it eventually results in a LOCK exception from RocksDB. – The root cause of K19994 is a `TimeoutExecption` from the clients, which Kafka Streams retires until it hits `task.timeout.ms` and gives up, but does not do a proper resource cleanup.

Not sure if it's the same thing you are hitting or not. K19994 should be independent of standby tasks though. Do you see any other exception before you hit the LOCK exception from RocksDB?
We see no other exceptions prior to the one above.
Reproduced with num.standby.tasks = 0 for the first time, please find attached the kafka-streams logs up until the error: no_standby_replication.log

Clarification: With num.standby.tasks = 0, we still get the error message "Some task directories still locked while closing state", but it seems harmless in this case. With num.standby.tasks > 0, subsequent Kafka streams startup also fails with the error message "lock hold by current process".

so far it looks like if we trigger a rebalance around the same time as a shutdown, we may leave some tasks not closed
it maybe somewhat related to https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-19831, but I am still investigating

what I found so far:

if we close a KS app while it's rebalancing and there was an active task that needs to become standby, it may never get closed:

here we add it to the pending tasks: https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/trunk/streams/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/streams/processor/internals/TaskManager.java#L814-L816
here we move pending tasks to the state updater: https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/trunk/streams/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/streams/processor/internals/TaskManager.java#L934 . if this happens, we close the tasks correctly during the shutdown step
but if the thread switched the state to PENDING_SHUTDOWN before we get there: https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/trunk/streams/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/streams/processor/internals/StreamThread.java#L1205-L1220, we will not close it.

nikita-shupletsov Thank you so much for fixing it! We will surely upgrade soon

fields.description:
Tiered storage fetch quotas are not properly enforced. Brokers can significantly exceed configured fetch quota limits because the quota check only evaluates historical usage and does not account for the size of the fetch request that is about to be executed.

The issues are:
 # Quota check happens BEFORE the fetch
 # The check only considers past usage
 # The fetch size is known but not considered
 # Actual bytes are recorded AFTER the fetch completes

*Example Scenario:*

  - Configured quota: 136 MB/s
  - Current usage (past 1 second window): 100 MB/s
  - New fetch request arrives requesting 50 MB

  *Current behavior:*
  1. getFetchThrottleTimeMs() checks: 100 MB/s < 136 MB/s → Not violated, returns 0
  2. Fetch proceeds and downloads 50 MB
  3. Total throughput: 150 MB/s → Exceeds quota by 14 MB/s
  4. quotaManager.record(50 MB) is called
  5. Next request will be throttled, but quota has already been exceeded

 

  *Expected behavior:*
  1. Quota check should evaluate: (100 MB/s + 50 MB estimated) = 150 MB/s > 136 MB/s → Violation
  2. Request should be throttled BEFORE fetching from remote storage
  3. Quota should never be exceeded

HI, [~mjsax] . 
I’ve looked into it and would like to discuss it with you.
 # In this PR([https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/16906)], it was decided to decommission ProcessorContext and use {{StateStoreContext}} instead of {{{}ProcessorContext{}}}. As part of this change, the internal field was changed from {{ProcessorContext}} to {{{}InternalProcessorContext<?, ?>{}}}.
 # {{MockProcessorContext.getStateStore()}} returns an anonymous {{{}StateStoreContext{}}}. However, this anonymous {{StateStoreContext}} is not related to {{InternalProcessorContext}} (note that {{InternalProcessorContext}} implements {{{}StateStoreContext{}}}).

At this point, since the anonymous {{StateStoreContext}} provided by {{MockProcessorContext.getStateStore()}} is not an {{{}InternalProcessorContext{}}}, an {{IllegalArgumentException}} is thrown.

There is a message saying, “This component requires internal features of Kafka Streams and must be disabled for unit tests.”{_}.{_}

What do you think?
Please let me know your opinion.

We had a similar issue in the past: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-10200

comments.body:
mjsax Hi!

If no one is working on this,, may I take a look?
Sure.

Thanks a lot.
Self assigned.

HI, mjsax . 
I’ve looked into it and would like to discuss it with you.

  1. In this PR(https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/16906), it was decided to decommission ProcessorContext and use StateStoreContext instead of ProcessorContext. As part of this change, the internal field was changed from ProcessorContext to InternalProcessorContext<?, ?>.
  2. MockProcessorContext.getStateStore() returns an anonymous StateStoreContext. However, this anonymous StateStoreContext is not related to InternalProcessorContext (note that InternalProcessorContext implements StateStoreContext).
  3. In InMemoryWindowStore.init(), ProcessorContextUtils.asInternalProcessorContext() is called. At this point, since the anonymous StateStoreContext provided by MockProcessorContext.getStateStore() is not an InternalProcessorContext, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.

There is a message saying, “This component requires internal features of Kafka Streams and must be disabled for unit tests.”.
However, I believe that the StateStoreContext provided by MockProcessorContext.getStateStore() is intended to be used specifically for testing Kafka Streams internal features.

Therefore, my opinion is that MockProcessorContext.getStateStore() should internally return an implementation that also implements InternalProcessorContext rather than StateStoreContext.

 

What do you think?
Please let me know your opinion.
I think this does make sense. We will need to carefully evaluate, how to implement all method of InternalProcessorContext correctly. But guess we can discuss on a PR?

Thanks for your comments! 
I see. I will create PR for discussing and let you know!

fields.description:
Kafka Streams allows users to configure many different memory limits, to pro-actively manage memory usage to avoid OutOfMemory errors.

However, on the restore code path, there is no such memory management. The `StoreChangelogReader` fetches a batch of message, and buffers them inside `ChangelogMetadata`, and there is no limit enforced on this buffer.

We could either re-use the existing config for input topic buffer (`
buffered.records.per.partition`) or introduce a new config (this would require a KIP though). – Even if we re-use the existing config, not 100% sure if we would need a KIP or not?

KIP-1325: [https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/KAFKA/KIP-1325%3A+Add+restore.buffered.records.per.partition+to+cap+Kafka+Streams+state-restore+memory]
fields.summary: Allow to configure max memory for restore path

comments.body:
Thanks a lot [~mjsax] for taking the time to bring this up. This is based on our observations while 'backfilling' state stores from a huge pile of pre-existing data. Specifically, we are implementing a CDC stack utilizing Debezium and Kafka Streams. Starting the streaming pipeline from scratch means to operate on pre-filled topics with millions of records before regular streaming starts. This backfill phase is extremely difficult to operate because even widely scaled out streams applications frequently die on OutOfMemory errors from restore buffers which can't be effectively controlled resource-wise.

A means to limit memory consumption of the restore path would vastly improve operability in case pipeline restarts are necessary for whichever reason.

I'd be happy to provide additional context or information if needed.

[~mjsax] I tried to look at this. 

So only in the normal processing path, streams enforce a buffer limit via buffered.records.per.partition (default 1000), but when restore happens, there is no such logic in RestoreChangelogReader.

Either we can apply the same config buffered.records.per.partition in RestoreChangelogReader, but 1000 looks low, as it can slow down restoration and we should also consider polling. If polling is faster and restore is slow, we notice a lag.

We can introduce a new config *restore.buffered.records.per.partition* default to a higher default 10000 may be. and the update the [restore()|https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/ccd8330e9eb0e2439f1d025282bef8b724d6ec1d/streams/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/streams/processor/internals/StoreChangelogReader.java#L438] method here

If you are ok, I can open a new kip
Sorry for late reply. Just working through may Jira notification backlog, now that AK 4.3 release settle down. – Sure, your proposal work for me.
https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/KAFKA/KIP-1325%3A+Add+restore.buffered.records.per.partition+to+cap+Kafka+Streams+state-restore+memory

[~muralibasani] [~mjsax] Is there anything I could help with here? We're having a painful backfill phase right now with frequent OOM crashes and the resulting rebalances and degraded performance, which reminded me of this issue. Please let me know if there is anything I could do to assist.

[~stoeckmk] a related PR [https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/22458] from kip-770 is under review.

After that, this kip-1325 would be resumed to follow the same bytes based approach.
[~muralibasani] Sorry for the late review! I've moved this to 4.5.0 since we're about to cut the 4.4 branch.
[~chia7712] thank you.

Hi [~stoeckmk],

Thanks for reporting this. I am helping [~muralibasani] with KIP-1325, and I am trying to find out which part of the restore path uses the memory in your case. Could you share a few details about your setup? Anything you can share helps, even if it is only part of it.

*Versions*
# Kafka Streams version, and Quarkus version.

*How the topology is built*
# In the Quarkus method that produces the {{Topology}}, do you return {{builder.build()}} or {{builder.build(props)}}? If you pass properties, does {{topology.optimization}} appear there?
# Do you see changelog topics named {{<application.id>-<store name>-changelog}} for the tables you read with {{streamsBuilder.table(...)}}?

*Kafka Streams configs* (from your {{application.properties}}, the {{kafka-streams.*}} part)
# {{num.standby.replicas}}, {{num.stream.threads}}, {{max.warmup.replicas}}, {{acceptable.recovery.lag}}
# {{processing.guarantee}}, {{commit.interval.ms}}
# {{statestore.cache.max.bytes}}, {{buffered.records.per.partition}}
# Any consumer overrides, in particular {{restore.consumer.*}}, {{max.poll.records}}, {{max.partition.fetch.bytes}}, {{fetch.max.bytes}}
# Any custom {{rocksdb.config.setter}}

*Size of the backfill*
# Number of partitions of the input topics, number of application instances, and the typical record size.
# JVM heap ({{-Xmx}}) and container memory limit of one instance.

*The OutOfMemoryError itself*
# When does it happen: on the first start of a new instance, while standby tasks are being updated, or when you scale out?
# Which thread throws it? The thread name in the stack trace (for example {{...-StreamThread-1}} or {{...-StateUpdater-1}}) would already tell us a lot.
# If you have a heap dump or a class histogram ({{jcmd <pid> GC.class_histogram}}), the top entries would be very helpful.

Thanks a lot!

Kafka Streams allows users to configure many different memory limits, to pro-actively manage memory usage to avoid OutOfMemory errors.

However, on the restore code path, there is no such memory management. The `StoreChangelogReader` fetches a batch of message, and buffers them inside `ChangelogMetadata`, and there is no limit enforced on this buffer.

We could either re-use the existing config for input topic buffer (`
buffered.records.per.partition`) or introduce a new config (this would require a KIP though). – Even if we re-use the existing config, not 100% sure if we would need a KIP or not?

KIP-1325: https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/KAFKA/KIP-1325%3A+Add+restore.buffered.records.per.partition+to+cap+Kafka+Streams+state-restore+memory

PR opened: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23024

Prevented premature ISR expansion under min ISR by requiring the follower to satisfy the existing caught-up check, while preserving leader-epoch expansion when the partition is not under min ISR. Added regression coverage for a follower that reaches the HWM but remains behind the leader LEO.

Update on PR #23024: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23024

The PR requires the existing caught-up check before expanding ISR while a partition is under min ISR, preventing a follower with only a stale high watermark from entering ISR prematurely. The non-min-ISR leader-epoch behavior is preserved.

renderedFields.description:
Thanks to mjd95 to report the following issue.

In the Partition.scala, the condition for the ISR expand and shrink does not match, which can cause a follower flapping in and out of ISR when:

  1. The partition is under min-isr which means the HWM can't advance.
  2. The replication is slow.
  3. The follower is far behind the LEO, but it is at/above the HWM.

Due to the "conflict" between the ISR expand and shrink:

  • Shrink ISR, attempted on a schedule, triggers if the follower's LEO has not recently caught up with the leader's LEO which takes the last caught up time into the consideration.
/**
 * Returns true when the replica is considered as "caught-up". A replica is
 * considered "caught-up" when its log end offset is equals to the log end
 * offset of the leader OR when its last caught up time minus the current
 * time is smaller than the max replica lag.
 */
public boolean isCaughtUp(
    long leaderEndOffset,
    long currentTimeMs,
    long replicaMaxLagMs) {
    return leaderEndOffset == logEndOffset() || currentTimeMs - lastCaughtUpTimeMs <= replicaMaxLagMs;
}

 

  • Expand ISR, attempted on processing follower fetch, triggers if the follower's LEO caught up with the leader's HWM in this fetch which only consider whether the replica reaches the HWM.
private def isFollowerInSync(followerReplica: Replica): Boolean = {
  leaderLogIfLocal.exists { leaderLog =>
    val followerEndOffset = followerReplica.stateSnapshot.logEndOffset
    followerEndOffset >= leaderLog.highWatermark && leaderEpochStartOffsetOpt.exists(followerEndOffset >= _)
  }
}

fields.description: Transaction V2 introduces frequent state transitions (epoch bumps) that briefly reject concurrent requests with CONCURRENT_TRANSACTIONS. The default client retry backoff (100ms) is excessive for these transient locks, leading to unnecessary latency and degraded throughput. Reducing the backoff allows faster retries and smoother performance during state transitions.
fields.summary: Optimize retry backoff for CONCURRENT_TRANSACTIONS to improve TV2 throughput

comments.body: The simple improvement is to modify TxnOffsetCommitHandler in TransactionManager.java. When receiving CONCURRENT_TRANSACTIONS, override the default retryBackoffMs with a smaller fixed value (e.g., 20ms) to expedite retries, similar to the existing logic in AddPartitionsToTxnHandler
ping [~jolshan]

Hey, I think this backoff is somewhat dependent on the system right? Depending on how quickly inter-broker requests occur 20ms could be too frequent as well right? For AddPartitionsToTxnHandler we had a config. Is this not working correctly for offset commits?

From KIP-890:

> Feb 2025. Adding additional configs to address a performance issue KAFKA-18654. During the transaction commit phase, it is normal to find CONCURRENT_TRANSACTION error when adding partitions to the transaction, because it takes some time for the markers to be fully propagated to all the data partitions. On the other hand, the client no longer sends the AddPartitionToTxn directly to the transaction coordinator, instead, the server sends the request as a part of the Produce/TxnOffsetCommit request handling. This new behavior causes the client to retry expensive produce requests during the transaction commit phase. So, we decided to let the server retry the AddPartitionToTxn when hitting the CONCURRENT_TRANSACTION. Then, the following 2 configs are used to control the retry.
 * _add.partitions.to.txn.retry.backoff.max.ms_ defines the maximum retry timeout when the server attempts to add the partition to the transaction.
 * _add.partitions.to.txn.retry.backoff.ms_ defines how frequently the server will retry the AddPartitionToTxn.

Reading the thread, I think introducing 2 new configs make sense. It solves the unnecessarily long backoff, but also addresses the system dependent aspect. [~chia7712], are you planning on implementing this? I would love to take a stab it otherwise!

[~francisgodinho] Sure. It is great to see more Kafka contributors :)

BTW, [~jolshan]'s feedback is usually very constructive for the KIP, so let's wait for her

Thanks [~chia7712] and [~francisgodinho] !
I think the main thing I'm concerned about with the two configs is adding more configs with limited scope. It would be nice to reuse the existing config for both types of requests, but it is unfortunate the naming isn't totally clear. (Under the hood, both produce and txnOffsetCommit use add partitions for tv2, but that's not obvious) 

Thoughts on reusing the same config but applying it with the other request?

renderedFields.description: Transaction V2 introduces frequent state transitions (epoch bumps) that briefly reject concurrent requests with CONCURRENT_TRANSACTIONS. The default client retry backoff (100ms) is excessive for these transient locks, leading to unnecessary latency and degraded throughput. Reducing the backoff allows faster retries and smoother performance during state transitions.

comments.body: The simple improvement is to modify TxnOffsetCommitHandler in TransactionManager.java. When receiving CONCURRENT_TRANSACTIONS, override the default retryBackoffMs with a smaller fixed value (e.g., 20ms) to expedite retries, similar to the existing logic in AddPartitionsToTxnHandler
ping jolshan

From KIP-890:

> Feb 2025. Adding additional configs to address a performance issue KAFKA-18654. During the transaction commit phase, it is normal to find CONCURRENT_TRANSACTION error when adding partitions to the transaction, because it takes some time for the markers to be fully propagated to all the data partitions. On the other hand, the client no longer sends the AddPartitionToTxn directly to the transaction coordinator, instead, the server sends the request as a part of the Produce/TxnOffsetCommit request handling. This new behavior causes the client to retry expensive produce requests during the transaction commit phase. So, we decided to let the server retry the AddPartitionToTxn when hitting the CONCURRENT_TRANSACTION. Then, the following 2 configs are used to control the retry.

  • add.partitions.to.txn.retry.backoff.max.ms defines the maximum retry timeout when the server attempts to add the partition to the transaction.
  • add.partitions.to.txn.retry.backoff.ms defines how frequently the server will retry the AddPartitionToTxn.

AddPartitionsToTxnHandler we had a config. Is this not working correctly for offset commits?

Depending on how quickly inter-broker requests occur 20ms could be too frequent as well right?

fields.description:
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-10386 we introduced Type.COMPACT_RECORDS in SchemaGenerator. However, we forgot to add Type.COMPACT_RECORDS to ApiKeys.retainsBufferReference(). This can cause the buffer in MemoryPool to be released too early, leading the data corruption and potential other weird problems. 

 

This issue is already fixed via https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-19634, but the changes are large. We probably should just fix the issue in ApiKeys.retainsBufferReference() in 4.2.0 and earlier versions.
fields.summary: Buffer released too early in MemoryPool

comments.body: There is another issue related to buffer release (KAFKA-19123). Perhaps we can fix them together in that patch

This doesn't seem to create a real issue since ApiKeys.requiresDelayedAllocation is set across all versions of Schema. So, as long as one version of the schema contains Type.RECORDS, ApiKeys.requiresDelayedAllocation is set correctly. An existing test ProtoUtilsTest covers the relevant schemas and didn't break.
This issue is not causing a real problem in 4.2.0. If it becomes a problem in the future, an existing test will expose the problem. So, closing it for now.

[~junrao] Should we move the logic to the generator instead of hardcoding the type list in ApiKeys? The generator could add a {{retainsBufferReference}} method to {{{}ApiMessageType{}}}, computed from the {{zeroCopy}} flag and {{records}} fields in the spec. That was actually cmccabe's original suggestion in #7342: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/7342#issuecomment-543979048

fields.description:
Hello，During my usage of Kafka, I identified an issue. In the {{kafka-server-start.bat}} script, there is a logic that sets different startup parameters based on the bitness (32-bit/64-bit) of the operating system. The relevant code is as follows:
{code:java}
IF ["%KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS%"] EQU [""] (
    rem detect OS architecture
    wmic os get osarchitecture | find /i "32-bit" >nul 2>&1
    IF NOT ERRORLEVEL 1 (
        rem 32-bit OS
        set KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS=-Xmx512M -Xms512M
    ) ELSE (
        rem 64-bit OS
        set KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS=-Xmx1G -Xms1G
    )
) {code}
It first queries wmic os get osarchitecture, then determines whether the operating system is 32-bit or 64-bit by checking if the result contains the string "32-bit". However, my actual tests show that this method is not reliable—the returned results vary across Windows systems with different languages and regional settings, as shown below:

 

{*}English Windows{*}:

!image-2025-12-30-16-27-52-195.png!

{*}Chinese Windows{*}:
!image-2025-12-30-16-28-25-539.png!



{*}French Windows{*}:

!image-2025-12-30-16-28-42-798.png!

{*}German Windows{*}:

!image-2025-12-30-16-29-03-343.png!

{*}Japanese Windows{*}:

*!image-2025-12-30-16-29-19-289.png!*

{*}Older Windows XP systems{*}:

!image-2025-12-30-16-29-36-542.png!

Kafka has users across the globe, and the current approach lacks universality.

comments.body:
[~mattmemobank] 
Do you mean that your controller fail to reload cert?
what's your controller work mode? Dynamic quorum or  Static quorum
For example
Dynamic quorum environment:
{{controller.quorum.bootstrap.servers=ip1:port,ip2:port,ip3:port }}
Static quorum environment:
{{controller.quorum.voters=id1@ip1:port,id2@ip2:port,id3@ip3:port}}

{{ }}And what's your command for kafka-configs.sh?

We don't have the issue in static quorum for cert reload.

[~fujian1115] 

??  Do you mean that your controller fail to reload cert???

No, we don't have any errors when reloading the certs. The issue comes when we restart the controllers and the broker needs to open new connections. It tries but with an old certificate, the one present at the start of the process. And because it tries to connect with an expired certificate, controllers are rejecting the connection with a {{{}CertificateExpiredException{}}}.

 

??what's your controller work mode? Dynamic quorum or  Static quorum??

My controller is configured as static quorum ({{{}controller.quorum.voters{}}}).

 

??what's your command for kafka-configs.sh???

We are using the following command to reload our broker certificates:
{color:#0073bf}kafka-configs.sh{color} \

{color:#067d17}--command-config /etc/kafka/kafka-broker-acl-client.properties {color}\--alter \

renderedFields.description:
Hi,

I'd like to discuss a gap in the dynamic SSL reconfiguration support for KRaft mode that affects brokers connecting to the controller quorum.

In KRaft mode, when SSL certificates are renewed and dynamically reloaded via kafka-configs.sh, the KafkaRaftClient (used by brokers to fetch cluster metadata from controllers as "observers" per KIP-853) does not pick up the new certificates.

This causes SSL handshake failures with CertificateExpiredException errors, even though the reload command reports success.

 

Error observed on broker:    org.apache.kafka.common.errors.SslAuthenticationException: Failed to
process post-handshake messages
    Caused by: javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: Received fatal alert:
certificate_unknown

Error observed on controller:
    Caused by: java.security.cert.CertificateExpiredException: NotAfter:
Wed Dec 17 08:28:22 UTC 2025

The SslChannelBuilder implements ListenerReconfigurable and supports
dynamic SSL reconfiguration. However, in KafkaRaftManager, the channel builder is never registered with config.addReconfigurable().

In contrast, NodeToControllerChannelManager (and other components) correctly registers the channel builder:
NodeToControllerChannelManager.scala (trunk, lines 130-132):

    channelBuilder match {
      case reconfigurable: Reconfigurable =>
config.addReconfigurable(reconfigurable)
      case _ =>
{{    }}}

I checked that the issue exists in both Kafka 3.9.1 and current trunk (as
of 2025-12-17).

The only reliable workaround I found is to restart the Kafka broker when
certificates are renewed. Has anyone else encountered this, or is there a reason this was intentionally left out?

Static quorum environment:
controller.quorum.voters=id1@ip1:port,id2@ip2:port,id3@ip3:port

from: [https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/15516#discussion_r2649600413]

The {{LogCleaner}} can fail with {{java.lang.IllegalArgumentException}} when the compacted data exceeds the segment size limit.

This issue occurs because the cleaner rebuilds batches using the default compression level. If the data was originally ingested with a higher compression level, the re-compressed batch size increases, causing the cleaner's size estimation to be inaccurate and leading to an overflow.

To address this without major architectural changes (like splitting segments during cleaning), we should introduce a safety margin or adaptive logic for partitions that encounter this overflow.
fields.summary: Handle LogCleaner segment overflow caused by compression level changes

This ticket tracks the work for KIP-1267.

The goal is to introduce consumer-level cost attribution metrics for Tiered Storage (KIP-405). currently, operators cannot distinguish which consumer group is responsible for remote storage fetch costs (S3 GETs/Egress). fields.description:
We've seen some occurrences of producer.flush hanging indefinitely in situations where a topic is deleted and the producer is using transactions v1

In the case where the producer has records in the buffer, and the topic deletion happens right before adding the first partition to the transaction, we could fall in a loop where the AddPartitionsToTx fails with a retriable error, and is continuously retried. In this case, none of the timeouts related to send, transactions or request seem to apply:
 * [transaction.timeout.ms|http://transaction.timeout.ms/] -> not applied because no partition has been added yet
 * [delivery.timeout.ms|http://delivery.timeout.ms/] -> not applied because the client does not attempt sending (where batching expiration applies) while it's in a transactional request (i.e AddPartitionsToTx), early return here [https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/3d267d45369818c804ed49c56e9ae405e28b234c/clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/clients/producer/internals/Sender.java#L333-L335])
 * [request.timeout.ms|http://request.timeout.ms/] -> not applied because it's not a request failure really, the high level operation too add partitions is retried.
 * [default.api.timeout.ms|http://delivery.timeout.ms/] does not apply to the producer.flush api by design (or to any produce request really)

Client handing of retriable errors when adding partitions to tx (this would be the case of UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION when a topic is deleted):

[https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/3d267d45369818c804ed49c56e9ae405e28b234c/clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/clients/producer/internals/TransactionManager.java#L1603-L1605]

This only affects producers using tx v1, and it's solved with tx v2 (partitions not added to the tx separately, so delivery timeout checked on send and applied, unblocking the flush operation).
fields.summary: Producer using transactions v1 could hang on flush upon retriable failures adding partitions to tx

comments.body:
[~lianetm] HI!

Are you planning to handle this yourself, or ask someone specific to look into it? If not, would it be okay if I take a look?

Hi [~chickenchickenlove] ,sure, we're not actively working on a fix. Just for context, this is something that is fixed with the v2 tx protocol (this, and many other transaction-related issues) so upgrading to use is probably the best path forward when dealing with this kind of situation. Then I'm not sure what would be safe fix for this edge case on v1 really. Any change would have to consider all the timeouts already involved, that would have to remain respected as now. It gets tricky given that some timeouts are controlled/enforced by the client, others by the broker (where I expect we don't want to change anything around this, it's v2 already the one redefining this path). But surely interesting to look into it in case we can think of a fix that is worth pursuing. Thanks!
[https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/21672]
[~lianetm]  I have done the changes, can you please review.

To build Docker images we first need to trigger the "Docker Build Test Workflow" Action for both jvm and native, and if successful then trigger the "Build and Push Release Candidate Docker Image" Action again for both jvm and native. Then we need to check that the tags are on dockerhub.

All of these steps could be automated and run for example in another GitHub Action.

fields.description:
The current {{docker_sanity_test.py}} only verifies "Combined" and "Isolated" modes, which inject all Kafka configurations (e.g., {{{}KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES{}}}) via environment variables.

This approach *masks regressions* where the default {{server.properties}} embedded in the image is corrupted or missing (such as the recent {{KAFKA_URL}} bug). The test suite effectively "fixes" the broken default config by overwriting it at runtime.

fields.description:
CREATE_TOPICS request currently checks whether a topic already exists before creating one. If a topic with the same name already exists, it will return a [TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS|https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/62206cfc5461629818a34723fee7817b369a6f7e/clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/common/protocol/Errors.java#L256] error code. No other information in the [CreateTopicsResponse|https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/62206cfc5461629818a34723fee7817b369a6f7e/clients/src/main/resources/common/message/CreateTopicsResponse.json#L42] is set if this topic already exists.

comments.body:
PR opened: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23052

Implemented KAFKA-20101 by supporting an explicit * wildcard in org.apache.kafka.sasl.oauthbearer.allowed.urls. The wildcard is scoped to the URL allow-list; org.apache.kafka.sasl.oauthbearer.allowed.files remains exact-match only. Added documentation describing the opt-in and its security implications.

Validation: TDD RED reproduced the pre-fix failure, then the focused regression tests passed after the fix. The full ConfigurationUtilsTest and full clients test passed. Checkstyle, SpotBugs, Spotless, and git diff --check passed. Status: PR open and awaiting maintainer review; not merged.
PR #23052 is open and ready for maintainer review: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23052

renderedFields.description:
With Kafka 4.0.0+ and https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/18519, using {{sasl.mechanism=OAUTHBEARER }}requires to whitelist the value of 

sasl.oauthbearer.token.endpoint.url by setting the Java system property -Dorg.apache.kafka.sasl.oauthbearer.allowed.urls at JVM startup.

https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/security/authentication/sasl/oauthbearer/configure-clients.html mentions  org.apache.kafka.sasl.oauthbearer.allowed.urls=*

This property specifies a comma-separated list of allowed IdP JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) and token endpoint URLs. Use * (asterisk) as the value to allow any endpoint.

org.apache.kafka.sasl.oauthbearer.allowed.urls=*

You should consult the specific Kafka client and IdP documentation for the exact interpretation and security implications of such a broad setting.

{}But this configuration doesn't appear to work with kafka-client / kafka-streams 4.1.1.

Debugging the code, the logic is to do an exact match between both strings (https://github.com/apache/kafka/blame/74ebbae8ece464573c1288e8f233ef804074fe7b/clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/common/security/oauthbearer/internals/secured/ConfigurationUtils.java#L407).

It would help to have such mechanism, to avoid duplicating the endpoint URL as a system property, which is error-prone. In container-based environments, the Kafka client configuration is immutable, and the assumptions of  CVE-2025-27817 that "Kafka Clients configurations can be specified by an untrusted party" are not applicable.

fields.description:
Implement configurable retry parameters for the +KafkaStatusBackingStore+ to address the TODO comment "retry more gracefully and not forever" and provide operators with control over retry behavior during transient failures.
h3. Problem Statement

 
KafkaStatusBackingStore currently retries status updates indefinitely when encountering retriable exceptions. This behavior is problematic because:
 # *Infinite retry loops* can cause the worker to become unresponsive during extended Kafka broker outages
 # *No visibility* into retry behavior - operators cannot tune retry parameters based on their environment
 # *Resource exhaustion* - indefinite retries can consume threads and memory during prolonged failures
 # *No graceful degradation* - the system continues retrying without bound rather than failing fast when appropriate

A TODO comment in the codebase ({{{}// TODO: retry more gracefully and not forever{}}}) explicitly acknowledges this issue needs addressing.
h3. Proposed Solution

Add four new configuration properties under the {{status.storage.}} prefix to control retry behavior:

 
||Property||Type||Default||Description||
|{{status.storage.retry.max.retries}}|INT|5|Maximum number of retry attempts before giving up|
|{{status.storage.retry.initial.backoff.ms}}|LONG|300|Initial backoff delay in milliseconds|
|{{status.storage.retry.max.backoff.ms}}|LONG|10000|Maximum backoff delay cap in milliseconds|
|{{status.storage.retry.backoff.multiplier}}|DOUBLE|2.0|Multiplier applied to backoff after each attempt|

The retry mechanism uses *exponential backoff with jitter* to prevent thundering herd problems during cluster recovery.
h4. Behavior
 * Retries occur only for exceptions marked as {{RetriableException}}
 * After exhausting {{{}max.retries{}}}, the operation logs an error and terminates gracefully
 * All retry attempts are logged at WARN level with attempt count and delay information
 * Non-retriable exceptions fail immediately without retry
 *  

h3. Benefits
 # *Predictable failure modes* - Workers eventually give up and surface errors instead of hanging
 # *Operator control* - Tune retry behavior based on environment characteristics
 # *Better observability* - Clear logging of retry attempts and outcomes
 # *Backward compatible* - Default values maintain similar behavior to current implementation

fields.description:
When {{ClassicKafkaConsumer.currentLag()}} is called, {{SubscriptionState.requestPartitionEndOffset()}} is called, which sets a per-partition flag named {{endOffsetRequested}}. This flag is later cleared by {{SubscriptionState.updateLastStableOffset()}}/{{SubscriptionState.updateHighWatermark()}} when a successful {{LIST_OFFSETS}} call is received. However, if the partition has an error code in the response, or the {{LIST_OFFSETS}} call itself fails, neither update method is called, and {{endOffsetRequested}} remains set. The problem is, on _any subsequent_ call to {{ClassicKafkaConsumer.currentLag()}}, the logic will see that {{endOffsetRequested}} is already set, and the offset request will be silently ignored.

The fix is to ensure that {{endOffsetRequested}} is cleared out even on failure cases.

Note: this is the companion ticket to KAFKA-20187 which affects the {{AsyncKafkaConsumer}}.

fields.description:
KIP-1142 introduced the LIST_CONFIG_RESOURCES RPC as a way of listing Kafka resources for which configuration properties can be described. It built upon KIP-1000 which was specifically concerned with client-metrics resources.
Unfortunately, this RPC requires DESCRIBE_CONFIGS permission on the cluster resource for all resource types. This has the side-effect that you need different permission to list groups (DESCRIBE on CLUSTER) than to list which groups have configs (DESCRIBE_CONFIGS on CLUSTER). This is an unintentional anomaly which leads to incomplete results for the kafka-configs.sh tool for users who only have DESCRIBE authority.
We need a KIP to examine the permissions required for each of the resource types and ensure that there are no such anomalies. Requiring DESCRIBE_CONFIGS on the CLUSTER to list client-metrics resources is fine, but it should probably be DESCRIBE on the CLUSTER to list the groups with configs (and then DESCRIBE_CONFIGS on the individual groups to describe the actual configs). Similarly, we should make sure that the behavior for topics and so on is sensible.
fields.summary: Authority for LIST_CONFIG_RESOURCES should be dependent upon resource type

fields.description:
# Summary
  When disabling remote log storage (`remote.storage.enable=true` → `false`) with
  `remote.log.delete.on.disable=true`, there is a race condition between
  `RLMExpirationTask` and `ConfigHandler` that can lead to premature deletion of
  local log segments, resulting in **data loss**.

 # Affected Versions
  Kafka 3.0+ (all versions with tiered storage support)

  # Severity
  Critical - Data Loss


  # Root Cause Analysis
  ## Simplified Flow
  Cancel Tasks → Reset Offset → [RACE!] → Task Updates Offset → Delete Data ↑___________________________________________|
  ## Key Issues
  1. **stopPartitions() returns immediately after canceling tasks** - does not wait
     for RLMExpirationTask to complete
  2. **Task cancellation is not checked during execution** - RLMExpirationTask
     continues running after cancel() is called
  3. **deleteRemoteLogPartition() executes before tasks stop** - while tasks may
     still be accessing remote storage

fields.summary: Data Loss Risk When Disabling Remote Storage Due to Race Condition

comments.body:
[~dyingjiecai]

Could you add more details on the data loss that you're observing?  If you want to preserve the remote data while disabling remote storag, then use {{remote.storage.enable=true,remote.log.copy.disable=true}} setting.

Hi [~dyingjiecai] 

I looked into this issue. Based on your logs, I think the mechanism may differ from the race condition described.

Your logs show
 - 15:14:37.184: \{{ReplicaFetcherThread-1-1}} increments logStartOffset to 3123750 ("leader offset increment")
 - 15:16:37.068: TS disabled, follower RLM task cancelled
 - 15:19:19.193: \{{kafka-scheduler-3}} deletes 30 segments due to "log start offset 3123750 breach"

The deletion appears to be triggered by the periodic cleanup scheduler acting on the logStartOffset that was set via normal follower replication, rather than a race between RLMExpirationTask and ConfigHandler.

Since \{{maybeIncrementLogStartOffset}} is monotonic (UnifiedLog.java:1369), the LSO=3123750 set at 15:14:37 cannot decrease after TS is disabled.
The subsequent cleanup then deletes local segments below this offset.

Could you share more context on the sequence of operations before 15:14:37?

For example, was this broker restarting, or was the partition being reassigned at that time?

As [~ckamal] mentioned, \{{remote.log.copy.disable=true}}  would be the safer path for this kind of transition. It might also be worth documenting that TS enable→disable may not preserve local data if the leader's logStartOffset has already advanced.

PR opened: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23025

Fixed remote-log cleanup cancellation ordering so an in-flight expiration task cannot publish a stale log-start-offset update after remote storage is disabled. Cancellation now interrupts and waits for task completion before partition cleanup.

Validation: RED reproduced the cancelled task advancing the offset to 100; GREEN regression and full RemoteLogManagerTest passed; storage Checkstyle, Spotless, and SpotBugs passed. Full :storage:check had one parallel timeout in TransactionsWithTieredStoreTest; isolated rerun passed.

Status: PR open and awaiting review.

Update on PR #23025: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23025

The PR serializes remote-log task execution with cancellation cleanup, waits for in-flight work before stopPartitions continues, and prevents stale expiration updates after cancellation.

The regression and RemoteLogManagerTest pass, as do affected static checks. The full storage check recorded one unrelated timing-sensitive timeout that passed in isolation. The PR is open and awaiting review.
PR #23025 is open and ready for maintainer review: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23025

1. Summary
    When disabling remote log storage (`remote.storage.enable=true` → `false`) with
    `remote.log.delete.on.disable=true`, there is a race condition between
    `RLMExpirationTask` and `ConfigHandler` that can lead to premature deletion of
    local log segments, resulting in *data loss*.
  1. Affected Versions
    Kafka 3.0+ (all versions with tiered storage support)
  1. Severity
    Critical - Data Loss
  1. Root Cause Analysis
    1. Simplified Flow
      Cancel Tasks → Reset Offset → [RACE!] → Task Updates Offset → Delete Data ↑___________________________________________|
    2. Key Issues
      1. *stopPartitions() returns immediately after canceling tasks* - does not wait
      for RLMExpirationTask to complete
      2. *Task cancellation is not checked during execution* - RLMExpirationTask
      continues running after cancel() is called
      3. *deleteRemoteLogPartition() executes before tasks stop* - while tasks may
      still be accessing remote storage

dyingjiecai

Could you add more details on the data loss that you're observing? If you want to preserve the remote data while disabling remote storag, then use remote.storage.enable=true,remote.log.copy.disable=true setting.

Hi dyingjiecai 

I looked into this issue. Based on your logs, I think the mechanism may differ from the race condition described.

Your logs show

  • 15:14:37.184: ReplicaFetcherThread-1-1 increments logStartOffset to 3123750 ("leader offset increment")
  • 15:16:37.068: TS disabled, follower RLM task cancelled
  • 15:19:19.193: kafka-scheduler-3 deletes 30 segments due to "log start offset 3123750 breach"

The deletion appears to be triggered by the periodic cleanup scheduler acting on the logStartOffset that was set via normal follower replication, rather than a race between RLMExpirationTask and ConfigHandler.

Since maybeIncrementLogStartOffset is monotonic (UnifiedLog.java:1369), the LSO=3123750 set at 15:14:37 cannot decrease after TS is disabled.
The subsequent cleanup then deletes local segments below this offset.

Could you share more context on the sequence of operations before 15:14:37?

For example, was this broker restarting, or was the partition being reassigned at that time?

As ckamal mentioned, remote.log.copy.disable=true  would be the safer path for this kind of transition. It might also be worth documenting that TS enable→disable may not preserve local data if the leader's logStartOffset has already advanced.

PR opened: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23025

Fixed remote-log cleanup cancellation ordering so an in-flight expiration task cannot publish a stale log-start-offset update after remote storage is disabled. Cancellation now interrupts and waits for task completion before partition cleanup.

Validation: RED reproduced the cancelled task advancing the offset to 100; GREEN regression and full RemoteLogManagerTest passed; storage Checkstyle, Spotless, and SpotBugs passed. Full :storage:check had one parallel timeout in TransactionsWithTieredStoreTest; isolated rerun passed.

Status: PR open and awaiting review.

Update on PR #23025: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23025

The PR serializes remote-log task execution with cancellation cleanup, waits for in-flight work before stopPartitions continues, and prevents stale expiration updates after cancellation.

The regression and RemoteLogManagerTest pass, as do affected static checks. The full storage check recorded one unrelated timing-sensitive timeout that passed in isolation. The PR is open and awaiting review.
PR #23025 is open and ready for maintainer review: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23025

### Summary
  When disabling remote log storage (`remote.storage.enable=true` → `false`) with
  `remote.log.delete.on.disable=true`, there is a race condition between
  `RLMExpirationTask` and `ConfigHandler` that can lead to premature deletion of
  local log segments, resulting in **data loss**.

  ### Affected Versions
  Kafka 3.0+ (all versions with tiered storage support)

  ### Severity
  Critical - Data Loss


  ### Root Cause Analysis
  ### Simplified Flow
  Cancel Tasks → Reset Offset → [RACE!] → Task Updates Offset → Delete Data ↑___________________________________________|
  #### Key Issues
  1. **stopPartitions() returns immediately after canceling tasks** - does not wait
     for RLMExpirationTask to complete
  2. **Task cancellation is not checked during execution** - RLMExpirationTask
     continues running after cancel() is called
  3. **deleteRemoteLogPartition() executes before tasks stop** - while tasks may
     still be accessing remote storage

# Summary
  When disabling remote log storage (`remote.storage.enable=true` → `false`) with
  `remote.log.delete.on.disable=true`, there is a race condition between
  `RLMExpirationTask` and `ConfigHandler` that can lead to premature deletion of
  local log segments, resulting in **data loss**.

 # Affected Versions
  Kafka 3.0+ (all versions with tiered storage support)

  # Severity
  Critical - Data Loss


  # Root Cause Analysis
  ## Simplified Flow
  Cancel Tasks → Reset Offset → [RACE!] → Task Updates Offset → Delete Data ↑___________________________________________|
  ## Key Issues
  1. **stopPartitions() returns immediately after canceling tasks** - does not wait
     for RLMExpirationTask to complete
  2. **Task cancellation is not checked during execution** - RLMExpirationTask
     continues running after cancel() is called
  3. **deleteRemoteLogPartition() executes before tasks stop** - while tasks may
     still be accessing remote storage

fields.summary: Implement lazy deserialization mechanism

comments.body:
I was just digging some code, and I am wondering if we can actually do this, w/o also being lazy for the value deserialization? To deserialize the value itself, we need to pass in `Headers` into `deserialize(...)` method, what implies we need to deserialize the headers, too. Or do I miss something? Or course, not all deserializers required access to headers, but not sure how we could decide what "type" of value deserializer we have, to apply this optimization for header-agnostic deserializers?

Also not sure if lazy value deserialization by itself would make sense? If not, it seems there is no opportunity to deserialize the headers lazily either. Thoughts? \cc [~alisa23] [~frankvicky] (and [~lucasbru] who proposed lazy deserialization on the KIP). If we strip out lazy header deserialization, also wondering if we would want to change the byte format and update the KIP?

[~mjsax] I think there is a way to optimize this so that we can avoid headers deserialization for headers‑agnostic applications (which I assume is the majority), but I agree that, in general, it’s not straightforward. We run into similar challenges in the changelogging layer (https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-20179). We might instead state that if a user wants to use headers‑aware stores, they need to accept the full cost. Of course, we should provide benchmarking results so users can see the overhead and make a more informed choice.

Regarding changing the byte format: should we really rule out lazy headers deserialization forever, or keep it open so we can potentially add an optimization later (implementing lazy deserialization for headers‑agnostic apps)?

[~frankvicky]  I see the change in the changelog stores (ChangeLoggingSessionBytesStoreWithHeaders, ChangeLoggingTimestampedKeyValueBytesStoreWithHeaders & ChangeLoggingTimestampedWindowBytesStoreWithHeaders) by extracting raw header bytes instead of fully parsing them into Headers objects. 

I also want to introduce a lazy SerializedHeaders wrapper (interface implementing Headers) that defers deserialization until the producer actually needs the header data, and supports add() (for vector clock entry) without deserializing existing headers. 

I do not see any other interface changes. 

Shall I try picking this up ? Do you think there are any blocking tickets to this?

[~shekharrajak] I see you have assigned the ticket to yourself and worked on a PR, while I have this discussion here. 

It could have been better if you ask here in the thread before working on it.

Btw, good work on the pr.
[~muralibasani], I apologize for the misunderstanding. I thought this was a discussion and missed seeing you want to open PR, but I will be more mindful moving forward.

[~shekharrajak] 

I left a few comments on the PR. Addressing them will also help keep this work separate from KAFKA-20179. We’re waiting on your response before moving forward. Thanks:)

fields.description:
The streams rebalance protocol \(KIP\-1071\) does not currently support static membership. Setting group.instance.id when using group.protocol=streams results in a ConfigException being thrown at startup \(see StreamsConfig.java:1507\-1508\). Static membership is an important feature for minimizing unnecessary task reassignments during planned maintenance or rolling updates.

As specified in KIP\-1071, static membership should allow streams clients to maintain stable identities across restarts. Members should be able to specify an instance ID in heartbeat requests, allowing them to rejoin without triggering full rebalances. When a member with static membership rejoins with updated configuration \(topology metadata, rack ID, or process ID\), the group epoch should be bumped but the member should retain its identity. The broker\-side infrastructure for static members already exists in StreamsGroup.java \(the staticMembers TimelineHashMap\), but the client\-side validation rejects the configuration and the coordinator logic to handle static member semantics is not complete.
fields.summary: Support static membership for Kafka Streams with the streams rebalance protocol

fields.description:
The streams rebalance protocol \(KIP\-1071\) does not currently support topology updates. If a topology is changed significantly \(e.g., by adding new source topics or changing the number of subtopologies\), users must create a new streams group. This is a significant limitation for applications that need to evolve over time.

As specified in KIP\-1071, topology updates should be supported through explicit versioning via a topology.epoch configuration. When a member joins with a different topology, the broker should compare epochs: if the epoch is the same but metadata differs, return STREAMS\_INVALID\_TOPOLOGY\_EPOCH; if the epoch is lower, return STREAMS\_TOPOLOGY\_FENCED; if the epoch is bumped by one, accept and update the group topology. Members with stale topologies should receive a STALE\_TOPOLOGY status in heartbeat responses but continue processing with their current tasks until upgraded. This enables rolling upgrades of the topology across application instances.
fields.summary: Support topology updates for streams groups without requiring a new group

comments.body:
Hi, [~lucasbru] !

If you are not working on this, May I take a look?

I'm happy to take it on!

Feel free to take a look. Note that there are some things to consider here:



 - What if KIP-1263: Group Coordinator Assignment Batching and Offload is used, and the topology is changed while an assignor is running concurrently.

 - Also related to KIP-1263 - we will have to get a new target assignment once the topology is updated. But the assignor may only finish asynchronously. What is the behavior in the meantime.

Thanks for the explanation!
I haven’t taken a deep look at KIP-1263 yet, but I’ll review it—especially the implementation details.

I belive KIP-1263 almost has been implemented!

So, let me look into this issue further. :)
Yes I agree. Generally, if we fail to reconcile the topology with the existing topics, the new target assignment should become empty and we should revoke all tasks from all members.

Thank you for your reply. I understand.

I checked and noticed that KIP-1263 has not been implemented yet. (https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/21727)
My understanding is that this change should be applied after the KIP-1263 implementation is in place. Is that correct?

If so, as you suggested, I will first think through what we can do in the meantime :)

Hi, [~lucasbru] !

 
While looking into this issue, I noticed a potential correctness problem during a topology update. I may be missing an existing safeguard, so I would appreciate your thoughts.
 
Assume that the *orders* and *clicks* topics have compatible partition counts.
With topology epoch 9, the group has two independent subtopologies: * *Subtopology 0* reads from {*}orders{*}.
 * *Subtopology 1* reads from {*}clicks{*}.

The current assignment could be: * Member A (topology {*}epoch 9{*}): *task 0_0* processes {*}orders-0{*}.
 * Member B (topology {*}epoch 9{*}): *task 1_0* processes {*}clicks-0{*}.

Member A then shuts down and releases its old task. It rejoins with topology epoch 10. In the new topology, the two sources are joined and copartitioned:
 * *Subtopology 0* reads from both *orders* and {*}clicks{*}.
 * The new *task 0_0* processes both *orders-0* and {*}clicks-0{*}.

During reconciliation, the following state may be possible:
 * Member A (topology {*}epoch 10{*}): new *task 0_0* processes *orders-0* and {color:#de350b}*clicks-0*{color}.
 * Member B (topology {*}epoch 9{*}): old *task 1_0* is still processing {color:#de350b}*clicks-0*{color} until it acknowledges its revocation.

 

The old and new tasks have different task IDs ({*}1_0{*} and {*}0_0{*}). Therefore, the normal cooperative handoff for the same active task may not make the new task wait for the old one. If task 0_0 is assigned before Member B has revoked task 1_0, both members could process clicks-0 concurrently using different topology versions.

This seems to suggest that preventing stale members from receiving new tasks may not be sufficient when a topology update changes the mapping between tasks and the topics used by their subtopologies, for example when subtopologies are merged or split.

I think the concern may not be limited to user source topics. A changed subtopology may also use repartition source topics, repartition sink topics, state changelog topics, and updated copartition groups. Old and new tasks may use the same internal topic partitions under different topology definitions. For example, repartition records produced by the old topology may be mixed with records from the new topology, or stateful tasks may write to or restore from the same changelog partition using incompatible state definitions.

One possible direction may be for the coordinator to retain enough information about the previous and current topologies during the transition. It could then delay an affected new task until any old tasks using overlapping source, repartition, or changelog topic partitions have been revoked.

Some of this transition information may also need to be persisted in __consumer_offsets so that the coordinator can safely recover after a failover instead of losing the relationship between the old and new tasks.

There may also be a sequencing issue if topology epoch 11 is introduced while the transition from epoch 9 to 10 is still in progress. It may be simpler to serialize topology updates and defer a new update until the previous rollout has completed, rather than retaining an unbounded number of topology versions and transition states.

I would appreciate your thoughts on this potential issue. If it seems valid, I can investigate the transition behavior further and prepare a small proof of concept to better understand the required changes. If the discussion shows that additional protocol or design changes are needed beyond KIP-1071, I would also be willing to work on a follow-up KIP.

 

What do you think? Thanks for reading this!

[~lucasbru]

Sorry to bother you.
When you get a chance, could you take a look?

Hey. I think you are right, there are corner cases we have to prevent from breaking things. That's why this ticket is non a standard implementation task but requires quite some investigation. I didn't have the time to look into this in detail. I expect to find some time in the coming weeks though. For now, I'd suggest you turn your attention elsewhere.

Hi, lucasbru!
I would like to get your opinion on one case. A topology update could turn two previously independent source topics into a copartition group. For example:

  // topology epoch 0
  KStream<String, Order> orders = builder.stream("orders");     // 3 partitions
  KStream<String, Click> clicks = builder.stream("clicks");     // 5 partitions

  orders.mapValues(...).to("order-out");
  clicks.mapValues(...).to("click-out");

After the topology update, the two streams could be joined:

  // topology epoch 1
  KStream<String, Order> orders = builder.stream("orders");     // 3 partitions
  KStream<String, Click> clicks = builder.stream("clicks");     // 5 partitions

  orders.join(
      clicks,
      (order, click) -> enrich(order, click),
      JoinWindows.ofTimeDifferenceWithNoGrace(Duration.ofMinutes(5))
  ).to("enriched-orders");

In this specific example, the new topology should fail the existing topology configuration/validation with INCORRECTLY_PARTITIONED_TOPICS, because the two external source topics in the copartition group have different partition counts. In that case, the task assignor is not invoked with the invalid topology; the configured topology is not ready and the target assignment becomes empty.

So I do not think this invalid copartitioning case needs special handling in the topology-epoch-aware assignment logic itself. Does that match your understanding?

fields.description:
The streams rebalance protocol \(KIP\-1071\) does not currently support pattern\-based topic subscription. Using regex patterns for source topics with group.protocol=streams results in an UnsupportedOperationException stating Pattern subscriptions are not supported with the STREAMS protocol \(see KafkaStreamsTest.java:1877\). This limits the flexibility of streams applications that need to dynamically consume from topics matching a pattern.

As specified in KIP\-1071, source topics should be specifiable using Google RE2/J regular expression patterns. The broker should resolve regex patterns against current topic metadata when processing heartbeats. If a regex matches zero topics or required source topics are missing, the group should enter NOT\_READY state with a MISSING\_SOURCE\_TOPICS status. The broker\-side data model already includes fields for sourceTopicRegex in the topology records \(see StreamsCoordinatorRecordHelpers.java\), but the actual resolution of regex patterns to concrete topics and the corresponding client\-side changes are not implemented.
fields.summary: Support regular expression topic patterns for streams groups

comments.body:
Hi, [~lucasbru] ! 

Are there any KIPs other than KIP-1071 that I should consider when addressing this issue? 
For example, in KAFKA-20170, I was told in a comment that I should consider both KIP-1071 and KIP-1263 together.
The only thing that comes to mind is KIP-848, KIP-1101. Nothing else comes to mind. Follow the implementation for consumer groups.

[~lucasbru] 

Thanks for your replying!

If you’re not currently working on this, would it be okay if I take it over?
If so, I’ll go ahead and self-assign this issue!

[~lucasbru] 

Gently ping...! 
Sorry to bother you. may I pick this up?

hey [~chickenchickenlove] . I think you could. But please note that I don't know yet how complex the implementation will be and it could be that reviews will take quite a bit of time.

cc [~lianetm] who is very familiar with the regular expressions logic in the consumer protocol.

[~lucasbru] 
Thank you for letting me know!
Yes, I will keep that point in mind as well.

If I run into any blockers or there are points I would like to discuss while working on it, I will mention Lucas and Lianet again and move things forward through discussion. In general, I plan to proceed with KIP-1071 and KIP-848 as the main references.

[~lucasbru]

I have a question regarding regex source topic resolution in the Streams protocol!

My understanding is that in the legacy Streams protocol, regex subscriptions are resolved on the client side into concrete topic names, and then the leader client’s assignor performs task assignment based on those resolved topics.

In contrast, KIP-1071 seems to suggest that in the new Streams protocol, regex subscriptions would be resolved on the broker side, with the broker returning the assignment in the heartbeat response.

With that in mind, would you expect us to support both client-side and broker-side resolution for backward compatibility, or would it make more sense for this ticket to implement only broker-side resolution and leave client-side compatibility support to KAFKA-20172?

 

For reference, a somewhat similar distinction appears to exist in the KIP-848 consumer protocol:
 * consumer.subscribe(Pattern) - Resolve topics matching the regex on client-side.
 * consumer.subscribe(SubscriptionPattern) - Resolve topics matching the regex on broker-side.

 

My personal inclination is that it would be better for the Streams protocol to support  broker-side resolution only. This seems more aligned with the direction described in KIP-1071, and it would also make the implementation simpler.

 

I’d appreciate your thoughts on this.

[~lucasbru] [~cadonna] [~mjsax] [~lianetm] 

Sorry for the wide mention!

I’d like to check whether I’m understanding the flow correctly and ask about one design concern while implementing regex source topic partition handling.

My current understanding is as follows:
 * A client may send both {{sourceTopics}} and {{sourceTopicRegex}} in the topology of the {{{}StreamsGroupHeartbeatRequest{}}}.
 * The broker can resolve the regex subscriptions into concrete topics and create tasks from those resolved topics.
 * In {{{}StreamsGroupHeartbeatResponse{}}}, the broker returns {{{}activeTasks{}}}, {{{}standbyTasks{}}}, and {{{}warmupTasks{}}}, but these only contain {{subtopologyId}} and {{{}partition{}}}, not the concrete topic information used to derive the assignment.

 

This seems fine when a subtopology contains only literal source topics, since the client already knows the source topic set for each subtopology and can reconstruct the corresponding {{{}TopicPartition{}}}s from the partition number.

However, with regex source topics, this is less clear to me.

The broker may resolve the regex and build tasks from the resolved concrete topics, but the client does not seem to know exactly which concrete topics were used. If the response only contains {{{}TaskId(subtopologyId, partition){}}}, I am not sure how the client can deterministically reconstruct the exact set of {{{}TopicPartition{}}}s it should fetch.

One possible approach would be for the client to resolve the regex on its side as well. However, that seems risky because the client and broker may observe metadata at slightly different times and therefore resolve different topic sets. In that case, the client could interpret the assignment differently from the broker.

Because of that, it seems to me that for regex source topics, the broker-resolved concrete topics need to be the source of truth for interpreting the assignment.

However, I could not find a field in the current {{StreamsGroupHeartbeatResponse}} schema that would let the broker return the resolved source topics per subtopology.

Am I understanding this gap correctly? If so, should regex source topic support require some way for the broker to return the resolved source topics in the response, or is there already another intended mechanism for the client to reconstruct the assignment deterministically?

I may be missing something, so I’d really appreciate any clarification.

Hey,

1) I agree, we should focus on broker-side resolution. In principle one can add client-side resolution as well, but I'm not sure it's going to be necessary. 

2) In principle it is correct that we may want to include topic IDs into the heartbeat response for KIP-1071 as well. However, I'm not sure this actually necessary or sufficient in the regular expression case. What we need to know, for a given record returned by the broker, which source node is going to consume it. It seems to me, that either way, we also have to evaluate the regular expression on the client side. Now, since the assigned resource here is a task, not a partition, it seems okay if the resolution does not give precisely the same result, as long as we can map partitions to tasks. Broker side, we cannot map the topic to a source node, so we'd have to bring the information "which source node is which regular expression" to the broker, which would require a broader RPC change (like using node IDs).

Hope that helps.

[~lucasbru] 

Thank you for the clarification and time! :)
This was very helpful and gave me a chance to look into the issue a bit more closely!!!

I may still be misunderstanding part of the intended flow, but I think my concern is slightly narrower.

I agree that the client likely still needs to perform the final topic-to-source-node mapping locally. 
In that sense, I do not think the broker necessarily needs to understand source node identity, 
and I am not yet convinced that introducing node IDs into the RPC is required for this specific issue.

My concern is earlier in the flow: how the client reconstructs the exact concrete TopicPartition set represented by an assigned task at a given moment.

With literal source topics, this seems straightforward, since the client already knows the exact source topic set for each subtopology. 
In that case, (subtopologyId, partition) is enough to reconstruct the fetch set.

With regex source topics, however, if the client is also allowed to resolve the regex independently from its own metadata view, 
it seems there may be race conditions in both directions.

First, the client may resolve faster than the broker.
 # Client1 discovers a new topic A-1 locally and resolves the regex.
 # Client1 starts treating its current tasks as including A-1 partitions 0-2.
 # The broker later resolves A-1, bumps the group epoch, and computes a new assignment in which Client1 should own only A-1 partitions 3-4.
 # Client1 then receives the new assignment and starts reconciliation.

In the window before step 4, it seems possible that Client1 could fetch, or even process, partitions that were never authoritatively assigned to it by the broker.

Second, the broker may resolve faster than the client.
 # The broker resolves A-1, bumps the group epoch, and computes a new assignment that includes A-1.
 # Client1 receives the new assignment, but its local metadata has not yet converged and it still does not see A-1.
 # Client1 cannot fully reconstruct the concrete TopicPartition set represented by the assigned task.

In that case, the client may either stall waiting for local metadata convergence, or acknowledge or materialize the assignment only partially.
However, as I understand KIP-1071, when the group epoch is bumped, a rebalance is supposed to follow. My concern is that, in this case, a rebalance might either proceed or fail to proceed regardless of the group epoch.

So my concern is not primarily that the broker must identify the source node. 
Rather, it seems that the client needs some authoritative broker-provided representation of the resolved concrete source topics that were used when interpreting the assigned tasks.

Would it be reasonable to consider extending the KIP-1071 heartbeat response schema with an optional field that returns the broker-resolved source topic names keyed by subtopologyId?

My thought is that this may be the minimal broker-authored information the client needs:
 # to reconstruct the exact concrete TopicPartition set intended by the broker, and
 # to still perform the final topic-to-source-node mapping locally using its own topology.

If such an extension is not desirable, I would also be very interested to understand what the intended authoritative source of that resolved-topic information would be on the client side, and whether there is already an existing mechanism that prevents the two races above...!

 

What do you think?

Nice analysis of the problem! I think the understanding just differs in whether the broker authoritatively assigns topic partitions, or just tasks.

KIP-1071 mostly thinks of the authoritative decision to be about tasks, while the client-side metadata defines which topics we are actually reading from. There may be a temporary mismatch - a task is created by the group coordinator that does not match any of the topics in the client-side metadata. Or a task is not yet created, even though the client metadata already contains a topic that has enough partitions to require such a task. But these should resolve by either an updated assignment from the broker, or a client metadata update, and I don't see problems created by these mismatches in the meantime. As you say, we'll still need to evaluate the regular expression client-side as well, to update sourceNodesByTopic. We also need to pull all metadata and update our assigned partitions when metadata changes. I don't see a correctness problem with this approach, but we will not really get the benefits of the broker-side regex resolution, since we are still mostly driven by the client metadata. 

There is an alternative solution, which would require an update to KIP-1071 or a small follow-up KIP, which is mostly what you mention - we include information about the topics in the heartbeat response, although I would use topic IDs, not topic names. This would allow us to only fetch metadata for the mentioned topic IDs to discover topic names. As long as we cannot resolve the topic ID to a topic name in our metadata, we will not fully reconcile the assignment. This is already done in the consumerMembershipManager, and the same could be done in the streamsMembershipManager. But even in this case, we'd need to evaluate the regular expressions client-side.

I think both approaches are possible, but the second solution is where we want to end up eventually, so I agree that it could make sense to introduce topic IDs to the heartbeat response at the same time or before implementing the regex support. Does this make sense to you?

[~lucasbru] 

Thank you very much for the detailed explanation! :)
I now realize that I had not fully internalized the point that, in this model, the broker is authoritative primarily over tasks. 
Your explanation helped me understand that distinction much more clearly.

I also agree with both of the approaches you outlined. 
In particular, looking at the first approach from the perspective of task assignment made it much clearer to me that this is not so much a correctness issue as a temporary mismatch that should eventually be resolved through assignment or metadata convergence.

I also agree that the second approach seems like the better long-term direction. 
In particular, returning topic IDs in the heartbeat response seems very reasonable to me. 
As I understand it, Kafka more broadly has been moving toward using topic IDs rather than topic names when handling cases such as topic deletion and recreation, where topic names alone are not stable enough(KIP-516). 
In that sense, this approach seems well aligned with that broader direction! :)

My understanding is that this model would help the client reconstruct the broker-intended concrete topic-partition view more precisely during reconciliation, 
while still leaving the final regex evaluation and source-node mapping on the client side. 
I also agree with your point that client-side regex evaluation would still be needed in this model. 
However, I understand its role not as independently determining assignment, 
but rather as mapping the broker-returned resolved topics to the appropriate source nodes in the local topology.

From that perspective, it seems to me that the work can be logically separated into two parts.
(1) extending the heartbeat response to include topic IDs per subtopology, and adding reconciliation support in StreamsGroup similar to ConsumerGroup.
(2) building regex support on top of that topic-ID-based mechanism.

I would appreciate your thoughts on whether it would make sense to handle the first part as a small follow-up KIP before KAFKA-20171. 

If that direction seems appropriate, I would be happy to draft it. If you let me know which direction you prefer, I will follow your guidance!

The streams rebalance protocol (KIP-1071) does not currently support pattern-based topic subscription. Using regex patterns for source topics with group.protocol=streams results in an UnsupportedOperationException stating Pattern subscriptions are not supported with the STREAMS protocol (see KafkaStreamsTest.java:1877). This limits the flexibility of streams applications that need to dynamically consume from topics matching a pattern.

As specified in KIP-1071, source topics should be specifiable using Google RE2/J regular expression patterns. The broker should resolve regex patterns against current topic metadata when processing heartbeats. If a regex matches zero topics or required source topics are missing, the group should enter NOT_READY state with a MISSING_SOURCE_TOPICS status. The broker-side data model already includes fields for sourceTopicRegex in the topology records (see StreamsCoordinatorRecordHelpers.java), but the actual resolution of regex patterns to concrete topics and the corresponding client-side changes are not implemented.
